concept_html:
A Delta table has a schema, and writes must match it. This is schema enforcement, and it is on by default. Tested on delta-spark 4.0.1:

Write Result
Append with an extra column Fails: schema mismatch
Append with a column missing Succeeds: the missing column is NULL
Append with a clashing type (INT into DOUBLE) Fails: DELTA_FAILED_TO_MERGE_FIELDS
Overwrite with a different schema Fails unless overwriteSchema is true
MERGE with updateAll/insertAll and an extra source column Succeeds, and silently drops the extra column

Enforcement is your friend. A failing write is a cheap, early signal that a delivery changed.

Schema evolution changes the table's schema to accept the new shape. Delta offers it per write:

  • Append: .option("mergeSchema", "true") adds new columns.
  • MERGE: .withSchemaEvolution() on the merge builder adds new source columns.
  • Planned change: ALTER TABLE ... ADD COLUMN (region STRING) in a reviewed migration.

Evolve on purpose, never by default. Two habits cause trouble:

  • Leaving mergeSchema on every silver write. A supplier typo such as final_wieght becomes a new, permanent column, and the real weight is NULL for that wave.
  • Setting spark.databricks.delta.schema.autoMerge.enabled for the session, which Databricks now labels legacy. It turns evolution on for every MERGE in the job, including ones you did not think about.

The safe pattern: validate the incoming columns against the registry first (lesson A2-L2). If a column is new and expected, add it with ALTER TABLE or evolve that one write. If it is unexpected, fail the run and ask the supplier.

Note the silent MERGE case in the table. Enforcement does not protect you there. Your column check does.

lines: def check_columns_match(df: DataFrame, expected: list[str]) -> None:
"""Fail when the delivery has unexpected or missing canonical columns."""
unexpected = sorted(set(df.columns) - set(expected))
missing = sorted(set(expected) - set(df.columns))
if unexpected or missing:
raise ValueError(f"schema drift: unexpected={unexpected} missing={missing}")
def append_wave(df: DataFrame, table: str, expected: list[str]) -> None:
"""Append after an explicit column check. Delta enforcement stays on."""
check_columns_match(df, expected)
df.write.format("delta").mode("append").saveAsTable(table)
def add_planned_column(spark: SparkSession, table: str, column: str, sql_type: str) -> None:
"""Planned schema change, run from a reviewed migration."""
spark.sql(f"ALTER TABLE {table} ADD COLUMN ({column} {sql_type})")

exercises.solution:
def schema_drift(actual: list[str], expected: list[str]) -> dict[str, list[str]]:
    """Compare delivered columns with the registry.

    Args:
        actual: Columns in the delivery.
        expected: Canonical columns from the registry.

    Returns:
        Sorted unexpected and missing column names.
    """
    return {
        "unexpected": sorted(set(actual) - set(expected)),
        "missing": sorted(set(expected) - set(actual)),
    }


def assert_no_drift(actual: list[str], expected: list[str]) -> None:
    """Raise ValueError when the delivery's columns differ from the registry."""
    drift = schema_drift(actual, expected)
    if drift["unexpected"] or drift["missing"]:
        raise ValueError(f"schema drift: {drift}")

def upsert_silver(spark: SparkSession, source: DataFrame, table: str, keys: list[str]) -> None:
    """MERGE a deduplicated source into silver."""
    spark.conf.set("spark.databricks.delta.schema.autoMerge.enabled", "true")
    condition = " AND ".join(f"t.{k} = s.{k}" for k in keys)
    (
        DeltaTable.forName(spark, table).alias("t")
        .merge(source.alias("s"), condition)
        .whenMatchedUpdateAll()
        .whenNotMatchedInsertAll()
        .execute()
    )

title: Schema enforcement is on by default. Evolve on purpose.
why_html:
A silver job appends with mergeSchema always on, "to avoid schema errors". A supplier's export misspells final_weight as final_wieght for one wave. The append succeeds. Silver gains a permanent final_wieght column, and final_weight is NULL for 2,000 respondents. Gold sums NULL weights to a smaller base, and weighted reach for that wave is computed on the wrong population.

Without mergeSchema, the append fails with a schema mismatch naming the unexpected column. The fix takes minutes, and silver never holds the bad wave.
